quickSummary: Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB: Lactobacillus, Lactococcus) ferment milk lactose into lactic acid, which partially digests and coagulates milk protein (Casein) into curd. Fermentation with inoculum starter enriches Vitamin B12 and provides probiotic protection in the human GI tract.

   Fresh Milk + Inoculum (Starter with millions of LAB)
                          │

                          │

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 1.1 Lactic Acid Bacteria (LAB) Mechanism
- **Taxa**: Microorganisms such as *Lactobacillus acidophilus*, *L. lactis*, and *Streptococcus thermophilus* (collectively designated **Lactic Acid Bacteria - LAB**).
- **Biochemical Reaction**: LAB grow in warm milk, fermenting the disaccharide sugar **lactose** into **lactic acid**.
- **Coagulation**: The generated lactic acid lowers milk $\text{pH}$ to acidic levels, causing the denaturation, partial digestion, and coagulation of the globular milk protein **Casein**, transforming liquid milk into semisolid **curd**.
- **Inoculum / Starter**: A small sample of previously set curd added to fresh milk at suitable temperatures ($37\text{--}40^\circ\text{C}$) contains millions of active LAB that rapidly multiply.

### 1.2 Nutritional & Probiotic Benefits
1. **Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ Enrichment**: Fermentation by LAB significantly enhances the nutritional profile of curd by synthesizing **Vitamin $\text{B}_{12}$ (Cyanocobalamin)**.
2. **Probiotic Gastrointestinal Health**: In the human stomach and intestines, LAB survive and establish beneficial colonies that competitively suppress the growth of pathogenic bacteria, maintaining a healthy gut microbiome.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Probiotics vs Prebiotics
conceptBreakdown.title: Probiotics vs Prebiotics
conceptBreakdown.content: Probiotics are live beneficial microorganisms (such as LAB and Bifidobacteria) that confer health benefits when administered in adequate amounts; Prebiotics are non-digestible dietary fibers (e.g., inulin, fructo-oligosaccharides) that selectively stimulate probiotic growth.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Other Fermented Milk Products
conceptBreakdown.title: Other Fermented Milk Products
conceptBreakdown.content: Beyond standard curd (Dahi), LAB fermentation produces specialized traditional dairy foods including Yogurt (fermented with Lactobacillus bulgaricus and Streptococcus thermophilus), Kefir (fermented with kefir grains containing yeasts and LAB), and Buttermilk.
